- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +15% above recent peak), apply a 10–15% downward correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.5–0.8), align forecast with 10-day moving average of history to dampen noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently >10% above true outcome, apply a 10–15% downward adjustment for next forecast.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) but price declines, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day of negative sentiment.
